algorithmic_comparison.formal_sce: SCE-UA (Shuffled Complex Evolution, Duan et al. 1992, 1993)
algorithmic_comparison.cma_es: CMA-ES (Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy, Hansen 2001)
algorithmic_comparison.evotorch: PyTorch EA / PGPE / SNES / CEM / GA

algorithmic_comparison.formal_sce: Uniform random sampling partitioned into q complexes of size m = 2p + 1
algorithmic_comparison.cma_es: Multivariate Gaussian sampling around mean vector with adapted covariance C and step sigma
algorithmic_comparison.scipy_de: Uniform random population of size popsize * N

algorithmic_comparison.formal_sce: Triangular probability simplex selection, reflection, contraction, random replacement per complex
algorithmic_comparison.cma_es: Weighted recombination of mu best candidates, cumulation path update for sigma and C
algorithmic_comparison.scipy_de: Vector difference mutation (v = r1 + F*(r2 - r3)) with binomial/exponential crossover

algorithmic_comparison.formal_sce: Periodic shuffling of all complexes into a single sorted population
algorithmic_comparison.cma_es: Single adaptive distribution; no complexes or shuffling
algorithmic_comparison.scipy_de: Single population with pairwise differential updates; no complexes
algorithmic_comparison.evotorch: Depends on algorithm; no SCE shuffling

algorithmic_comparison.formal_sce: kstop loops with relative change <= pcento or max_evaluations
algorithmic_comparison.cma_es: tolx, tofun, tofunhist, tolflatfitness, maxfevals, maxiter
algorithmic_comparison.scipy_de: relative tolerance tol, absolute tolerance atol, maxiter

algorithmic_comparison.formal_sce: torch.Generator(device=cpu) explicit manual_seed; strictly reproducible candidate sequence
algorithmic_comparison.cma_es: CMAOptions seed parameter; internal NumPy RNG

algorithmic_comparison.formal_sce: Native candidate batching along leading GPU tensor dimension [C, time, 3]
algorithmic_comparison.cma_es: Ask-and-tell interface allows user to batch-evaluate lambda candidates
algorithmic_comparison.scipy_de: vectorized=True passes 2D matrix [N, dim] to objective
algorithmic_comparison.evotorch: SolutionBatch._evaluate_batch natively supports PyTorch GPU batch tensors

level_a_direct_inheritance.reason: No installed package contains an SCE-UA class to inherit from. Subclassing CMA-ES or DifferentialEvolution would replace the required SCE-UA search algorithm with a completely different mathematical method.

level_b_composition_wrapper.verdict: suitable for experimental ablation only; prohibited for formal SCE protocol baseline
level_b_composition_wrapper.reason: CMA-ES or DE can easily be wrapped to call UnifiedEvaluator.score_batched as experimental calibration alternatives, but cannot serve as the paper-mandated SCE-UA baseline.

level_c_partial_internals_reuse.reason: The SCE-UA algorithm logic (complex partitioning, simplex evolution, shuffling) is already concisely implemented in project/autofuse/sce.py in ~150 lines of clean PyTorch code without external dependency baggage.

level_d_maintain_in_repo_sce.reason: In-repo SCEBaseline guarantees 100% adherence to Duan et al. (1992, 1993) SCE-UA, exact seed reproducibility, and zero-overhead coupling to the frozen Torch-FUSE v1 GPU batch kernel.

recommendation_summary: Maintain and use the optimized in-repo SCEBaseline (Level D). It strictly implements the intended SCE-UA algorithm specified by the FUSE paper protocol, achieves bitwise parity with frozen references, and exploits GPU candidate batching directly.
